text:
Ravi: hey everyone, new hire here. I can connect to WireGuard (split-tunnel) but when I sign into the internal web dashboard the OAuth redirect goes to the public login page and my session fails. Browser shows hostname resolves to our public LB IP instead of internal IP (10.4.x.x). Anyone seen this kind of dual-DNS/proxy race?
IT-ops: welcome! that sounds like a split-dns + PAC/proxy ordering problem. Which OS/browser are you using? Any corp MDM/profile applied?
Ravi: Windows 11 company laptop, Chrome. We have an auto-config PAC pushed by MDM for corp proxy and WireGuard profile from IT. I noticed the proxy PAC returns DIRECT for *.redwood.internal but system DNS still uses home ISP for some queries.
net-bot: Note: assigned wg ip 10.4.14.22, policy split-tunnel, pushed DNS 10.4.14.2 for internal domains. Detected active proxy.pac on system.
Megan: Chrome uses system proxy settings but also has its own DNS cache and can do DoH if enabled. Can you check `nslookup internal-dashboard.redwood 10.4.14.2` and then `nslookup internal-dashboard.redwood` (default)?
Ravi: ran them:
```
C:\> nslookup internal-dashboard.redwood 10.4.14.2
Server:  10.4.14.2
Address: 10.4.14.2#53
Name:    internal-dashboard.redwood
Address: 10.4.33.55

C:\> nslookup internal-dashboard.redwood
Server:  myhome.isp.dns
Address: 192.168.0.1#53
Name:    internal-dashboard.redwood
Address: 34.88.12.7
```
Ravi: so PAC expects DIRECT (internal), but normal resolver returns public IP. Chrome then tries the public IP and SSO redirects fail because the callback URL only accepts internal referer.
IT-ops: exact issue. Windows has per-connection DNS and Chrome might prefer system default resolver over the VPN DNS for some queries (especially if DoH or a browser resolver is enabled). Quick workaround: in Chrome go to chrome://settings/security and disable "Use secure DNS" (DoH) and clear host cache. Also test `curl --resolve internal-dashboard.redwood:443:10.4.33.55 https://internal-dashboard.redwood/` to confirm internal path works.
Ravi: `curl --resolve` worked and I could authenticate. Disabling secure DNS in Chrome also fixed it for a while.
Megan: For a durable fix we can tag your onboarding profile to push a PAC + hosts override and disable DoH for corporate-managed devices with `splitdns-pac-fix` tag (ticket ONB-5488). That pushes a local proxy/pac that forces internal names to 10.4 DNS lookup and creates local hosts entries for a small set of critical services.
Security: Quick note: we avoid adding long-lived hosts entries for auth services; we'll only add a short allowlist for first-week onboarding. We also prefer to turn off browser-level DoH centrally so internal DNS responses are authoritative.
IT-ops: To get you unblocked now I added tag ONB-5488 to your ticket. Also if you prefer, use the internal browser profile (Edge corp) we preconfigure for SSO flows — it enforces system DNS and proxy order.
Ravi: awesome thanks. One follow-up: how do I check if Chrome is using DoH from cmd line?
Megan: open chrome://net-internals/#dns to see host resolver cache and chrome://net-internals/#sockets to flush. For cmd we don't have a simple way; easiest is to check chrome settings or enterprise policy.
Ravi: fixed now using Edge corp profile. I'll leave this ticket open until DNS/DoH policy is applied more broadly. Thanks for the fast help and welcome :)
